## What I built

A hand-written scanner (no lookup tables) split by responsibility, all in the root `csv` package so `@csv.parse` / `@csv.print` resolve directly:

- `csv_parse.mbt` — `parse`: walks the input one field at a time with a cursor over UTF-16 code units. ## What I built

A general, streaming Protocol Buffers wire-format codec for MoonBit, implemented across four focused files in the root `protobuf` package (each well under the 1000-line limit):

- [readers.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/readers.mbt) — byte plumbing: `BytesReader`, `LimitedReader`, and the loop-until-complete helpers (`fill_once`, `read_exact_bytes`, `skip_bytes`).
- [varint.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/varint.mbt) — ten-byte-limit base-128 varints (non-minimal forms accepted, bits above the 64th dropped, eleventh byte = overflow) and minimal writers.
- [decode.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/decode.mbt) — keys, all 16 scalar readers, int32-bounded length prefixes, strict UTF-8 strings, `read_packed` through a `LimitedReader`, and `read_unknown` for wire types 0/1/2/5 plus recursive group skipping with matching end-tag checks.
- [encode.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/protobuf_run_1/encode.mbt) — the mirror-image typed writers, zigzag, sign extension, and bit-exact little-endian floats.

### Design
A character-driven state machine over the input's UTF-16 code units. Because `,`, `"`, `\n`, `\r` are all ASCII, they never fall inside a surrogate pair, so scanning by code unit and slicing the `StringView` at those boundaries preserves any Unicode content (emoji included). Layered as `parse_field` → `parse_record` → `parse`:
- Quoted fields collapse `""` to `"`; an unterminated quote or non-separator text after a closing quote raises.
- Unquoted fields reject an embedded `"`; `\` is ordinary text (so `"a\"b"` is rejected).
- Terminators `\n`, `\r\n`, `\r`; CRLF counts as one.
- Empty input → 0 records; a lone terminator → `[[""]]`; a trailing terminator adds no record.
- Rectangularity: all records must match the first record's field count.

`print` is the inverse (quote when a field has `,`/`"`/CR/LF or is empty; double `"` inside quotes; records joined by `\n`, no trailing terminator), so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds for every rectangular document.

- Record terminators `LF`, `CRLF` (single), and lone `CR`; empty input → zero records; a final terminator adds no extra record.
- Unquoted fields are one slice; a `"` inside them is rejected.
- Quoted fields copy runs between quotes and turn `""` into `"`; commas/newlines are literal; after the closing quote only `,`, a terminator, or EOF may follow (so backslash escapes and trailing text are rejected); an unterminated quote is rejected.
- Rectangularity is enforced (all records must match the first record's field count).
- `print` writes one `LF`-terminated line per record and quotes a field iff it contains `,`, `"`, `CR`, or `LF` (inner quotes doubled), making `parse(print(doc)) == doc` a total inverse on rectangular documents.
